purpose: R2 of the frozen 2-D cylinder control (cyl2d_contract.json 9d53cd1 + ddc7095; band cyl2d_band.json 5a02b46): n_D 64, H 60, Re 100, t_end 600, on one GPU (target: GCP g2-standard-4, one NVIDIA L4, 4 vCPU, 16 GiB host). Same equations, domain, boundary conditions, forces, averaging and band as R1/R3/M1 in the CPU packet 95ac40c9. Combined with those runs, R2 decides R2_fidelity and grid_pair.
science: model diagnostics; never 'passed'. eval.json here evaluates R2 alone (R2_fidelity and periodicity); control_passes needs R1, R3 and M1 from the CPU packet as well, combined by cyl2d_eval.py afterwards. The 3-D C1 sphere reference gate FAILED and stays failed. No fin, fish, swimming or flight claim.

reference_gate.C1_sphere_3d: FAILED (|Cd| 0.875 at D16 CPU, 0.918/0.881 at D32 GPU, vs band [0.95, 1.35]); blocks physical-validation wording
reference_gate.cyl2d: frozen contract + band; evaluator fails closed (a92d80e)

platform_note: R2 runs on CUDA (Float32, env_gpu pins) while R1/R3/M1 run on CPU (env Manifest). Same WaterLily 1.10.0 and Julia 1.12.7; the same-state control below measures the CPU/CUDA difference on one shared flow state before R2 starts.

env.note: the same pins and digest as the H100 fish packet 5af94b3f, which instantiated and passed its CUDA gate on 2026-10-31

export_note: off by default (export_bytes_max 0) for a 16 MB-return host; on GCS the dispatcher sets CFD3D_EXPORT_BYTES_MAX=2800000000: coherent R2 snapshots (~0.8 GB) every 3 h and at a stop-at-budget, listed in OUT/checkpoints/manifest.json, with 0.9 GB held for the stop snapshot; CFD3D_RESUME_FROM continues on another job

same_state.tolerance_units: Cd, Cd_p, Cl: max |difference| over the compared steps divided by the CPU mean |Cd|; t: max relative difference; u_abs: max |u_cpu - u_cuda| over the whole field after the continuation, U = 1
same_state.tolerance_basis: frozen before any CUDA run of this code; 0.005 is the GPU tolerance the earlier CUDA platform gate used (packet.json local_cpu_pins rel_tol_gpu) and passed with
same_state.mutant: the same comparison with the CUDA series shifted by 10 steps must NOT be within tolerance (shows the comparison can fail on a developed shedding flow)

calibration.rule: GO only if: TIMING rc 0 on the device; steps_projected[1] (340k, the developed-wake dt) x measured s/step x run_overhead 1.3 <= time left before the outer budget minus emit and checkpoint margins; nvidia-smi device-memory peak <= 0.8 x card total; host RSS peak <= 10 GB. Otherwise rc 11: stop with the controls, calibration.json and nvidia-smi kept; no R2 started. fits_time_lower_only reports when only the 204k-step projection would fit (a decision for root/infra, not taken here)
calibration.note: force-free TIMING; run_overhead 1.3 (forces every step, host copy of p every 10th step after t = 100) is an ASSUMPTION; R2's own wall_s and steps are the measurement

R2.l4_wall: NOT ASSUMED; measured by calibration. For orientation only: the L4's memory bandwidth (~0.3 TB/s) is ~1/11 of an H100's, and this solver is bandwidth-bound, so hours to tens of hours are plausible; the rule decides
R2.output: runs/R2.json.gz: t, Cd, Cd_p, Cl every step as shortest Float32 decimals (~14 MB raw at 340k steps, ~5-6 MB gzip)

outer_budget_note: default only; the dispatcher sets CFD3D_OUTER_BUDGET_S = VM hard stop - export margin. The calibration rule compares R2's projected wall time with what is left of it

host_requirements.caps: every Julia process tree <= 11 GB host RSS (systemd scope MemoryMax + MemorySwapMax=0 where available, and the RSS watchdog); the steps run one at a time
host_requirements.gpu: one CUDA device, driver supporting CUDA 12 (the pinned CUDA.jl 6.4.2 fetches its own runtime artifact)
